title: Week 2 Readout — Console Onboarding Nudges (Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint)
content:
Owner: Marissa (Console) | Experiment owner: Ben (Growth)
Week: Sprint Week 2 (Console nudges framework + first nudge experiment)
Date range covered: 2026-01-26 to 2026-01-30 (Mon–Fri)

1) TL;DR (what happened / what we decided)
- We launched v1 of in-console onboarding nudges behind feature flags with a holdout cohort.
- Best performer: “Create an API key” nudge (high CTR, high step completion, strong movement to first request).
- Solid: “Run your first request (Hello World)” nudge (good CTR; meaningful lift to first_success_request among exposed users).
- Mixed: “Enable streaming” nudge (good CTR, low completion; users unclear on why/when to use it).
- Weak: “View usage dashboard” nudge (low CTR; most users are not ready for cost/usage until after first value).
- Decision: Keep 2 nudges (API key + first request) and graduate them to broader rollout next week with UX fixes. Retarget/iterate streaming messaging. Defer usage dashboard nudge until post-activation milestone.

2) Hypotheses (from PM-663)
H1: Contextual nudges reduce time-to-first-token (TTFT proxy) by guiding users through the shortest “first value” path.
H2: Nudges increase 7-day activation (% of new signups hitting first_success_request + first_100k_tokens milestones).
H3: Nudges reduce drop-off at key funnel steps (API key creation, first request).

3) Experiment setup
Cohorts / targeting
- Eligible users: new Hosted API signups created after 2026-01-26 00:00 UTC, self-serve only.
- Exclusions: suspected enterprise pipeline / active opp domains per Sales guidance (handled upstream in lifecycle audience logic; for console we excluded users tagged sales_assisted=true in CRM sync where available).
- Regions: all, but note a known event ingestion lag in eu-west for ~6 hours on 2026-01-27 (see Data Quality).

Feature flags & holdout
- Flag: lifecycle_growth.console_nudges_v1 (ENG-10501)
- Assignment: 80% treatment / 20% holdout (sticky by user_id). No cross-over once assigned.
- Nudge frequency cap: max 1 “primary” nudge per session, 3 per week; dismissal persisted for 14 days.

Placement
- Primary location: Console home + API Keys page header area (contextual).
- Secondary: Model playground landing (only for “first request” nudge).

Nudge variants shipped (v1)
A) Create an API key
- Trigger: user has 0 API keys; viewed console home or /keys page.
- CTA: “Create API key”

B) Run your first request (Hello World)
- Trigger: has API key AND has not fired first_success_request; viewed home or playground.
- CTA: “Copy quickstart snippet” (deep link to docs + in-console snippet modal)

C) Enable streaming
- Trigger: first_success_request occurred AND streaming not enabled in last request; visited playground.
- CTA: “Try streaming”

D) View usage dashboard
- Trigger: first_success_request occurred; visited console home.
- CTA: “View usage”

Primary metrics (week 2)
- Nudge CTR = nudge_clicked / nudge_impressions
- Step completion rate (per nudge) = completed_target_step / nudge_clicked
- Downstream conversion (early signal) = first_success_request within 24h of nudge click; API key created within 1h

Secondary metrics / guardrails
- Support tickets mentioning “blocked” / “confusing onboarding”
- Rage clicks / repeated dismissals (qualitative proxy)
- Page load / console errors around nudge rendering

4) Results summary (directionally accurate; final numbers may shift slightly with late-arriving events)

Sample sizes
- New eligible signups in window: 4,812
- Treatment: 3,844 users
- Holdout: 968 users
- Users who saw at least 1 nudge impression (treatment): 2,907 (76% of treatment; remainder didn’t return to console)

4.1 Nudge performance (impressions → clicks → completion)

A) Create an API key
- Impressions: 6,120
- Clicks: 1,124
- CTR: 18.4%
- Completion (API key created within 1h of click): 812 / 1,124 = 72.2%
- Notes: Strong performance across all segments. Biggest drop-off comes from users who click but then hit org permission confusion (personal vs org workspace).

B) Run your first request (Hello World)
- Impressions: 4,985
- Clicks: 713
- CTR: 14.3%
- Completion (first_success_request within 24h of click): 286 / 713 = 40.1%
- Notes: Users respond well to “copy snippet” CTA. Completion rises to ~52% when the snippet modal is used vs deep-linking out to docs (suggests keeping them in-console reduces drop-off).

C) Enable streaming
- Impressions: 2,044
- Clicks: 241
- CTR: 11.8%
- Completion (streaming=true on next request within 72h): 39 / 241 = 16.2%
- Notes: Qual feedback indicates users don’t know why streaming matters unless they are already building UI. Language may be too generic and feels like “extra work”.

D) View usage dashboard
- Impressions: 2,312
- Clicks: 140
- CTR: 6.1%
- Completion (visited usage dashboard and stayed >10s): 62 / 140 = 44.3%
- Notes: When clicked, it’s fine. The problem is relevance/timing; too early in journey.

4.2 Downstream funnel movement (treatment vs holdout; early read)
These are early leading indicators; we do not have full D7 yet for late-week signups.

Within 24 hours of signup
- API key created
  - Treatment: 61.5%
  - Holdout: 55.9%
  - Absolute lift: +5.6 pp

Within 72 hours of signup
- first_success_request
  - Treatment: 34.8%
  - Holdout: 31.2%
  - Absolute lift: +3.6 pp

Median time from signup → API key created (among those who create a key)
- Treatment: 12.4 minutes
- Holdout: 16.8 minutes

Interpretation
- The lift appears driven primarily by the API key nudge and the “first request” nudge. Streaming + usage did not show meaningful near-term effect on activation.

5) Qualitative feedback (what users told us / what we observed)
Sources
- Office hours notes (Fri)
- Slack #product thread on dismissal persistence
- Support ticket SUP-24905 (nudge interfering with API key creation)

Themes
1) Clarity wins over breadth
- Users repeatedly asked for “the one thing to do next.” The checklist-y language worked best when it was extremely short and specific.

2) Keep them in the console
- Users who clicked a nudge and immediately left to docs were less likely to complete the step (esp. first request). The snippet modal pattern seems like a strong activation accelerator.

3) Dismissal behavior needs polish
- Complaint: “I dismissed it but it came back when I refreshed.” Root cause: dismissal persistence keyed by nudge_id + page_context; users saw the same nudge on a different surface and perceived it as “coming back.” (See Slack thread 1768591120.)

4) One high-severity bug (now mitigated)
- SUP-24905: A nudge state incorrectly overlaid / blocked the API key creation flow for a subset of users (likely due to z-index + loading state on /keys).
- Mitigation: hotfix rolled out 2026-01-30 18:10 UTC; added QA coverage for modal overlay conflicts.
- Impact: small but painful; likely affected <0.5% of treatment users, but created outsized frustration. Guardrail: if a nudge causes friction on a critical path step, we pause immediately.

6) Data quality / instrumentation notes
- Event taxonomy used: nudge_impression, nudge_click, api_key_created, first_success_request, request_streaming_enabled, usage_dashboard_viewed.
- Known issue: brief eu-west ingestion delay on 2026-01-27 resulted in undercounted impressions for ~6 hours; we corrected via backfill, but some joins may still be incomplete.
- Recommendation: add a dashboard alert for sudden drops in nudge_impressions by region to catch this earlier.

7) Decisions (keep / iterate / kill)
Keep (expand rollout next week)
- Create an API key nudge
  - Why: best CTR + completion; meaningful reduction in time-to-key.
  - Changes before expanding: improve copy around “You’ll need this for your first request” + add 1-line explanation of org vs personal keys.

- Run your first request (Hello World) nudge
  - Why: good CTR; completion strong when snippet is in-console.
  - Changes before expanding: make in-console snippet the default path; deep link to docs as secondary.

Iterate (retarget)
- Enable streaming nudge
  - Why: CTR OK but completion low; unclear value.
  - Next test: reframe to outcome (“Faster UI: stream tokens as they generate”) + target only users who have used the playground or have a front-end SDK detected.

Defer / remove from onboarding path (for now)
- View usage dashboard nudge
  - Why: low CTR early; not a “next best action” before first value.
  - Plan: reintroduce post-activation (after first_100k_tokens) as a cost-control nudge, potentially paired with “set a usage budget” or “view latency/cost breakdown.”

8) Follow-ups / action items
Product / Design
- (Kenji) Revise API key nudge microcopy + add org/personal clarification (ETA 2026-02-03)
- (Kenji/Marissa) Update first request nudge to prefer in-console snippet modal + better CTA label (“Run hello world”) (ETA 2026-02-03)
- (Marissa) Define post-activation nudge slot for usage/cost education (draft spec for Week 4 backlog)

Engineering
- (Dylan/Leila) Add regression test coverage for overlays on /keys and home (prevent SUP-24905 class issue)
- (Logan/Paula) Add region-level monitoring for nudge_impressions + missing events (tie into activation funnel dashboard)
- (Jada/Ethan) Confirm holdout integrity after hotfixes (no cohort leakage)

Growth / Measurement
- (Ben) Update weekly experiment scorecard with week 2 deltas + annotate known data gap window
- (Ben/Tyler) Align on what we’ll call “completion” for first request: 24h vs 72h window; propose standard for readouts

9) Open questions
- Should we move “first request” nudge earlier (immediately after API key creation) with a toast + persistent CTA on home?
- Do we need a “choose a model” guided default for first request, or is the default model selection already sufficient?
- If we keep nudges always-on, what is the right long-term cap (per session / per week) to avoid fatigue?

Appendix A — Copy as shipped (v1)
- API key: “Create an API key to start sending requests.” CTA: “Create API key”
- First request: “Make your first request in under 2 minutes.” CTA: “Copy quickstart snippet”
- Streaming: “Enable streaming for better UX.” CTA: “Try streaming”
- Usage: “Track tokens and cost in the usage dashboard.” CTA: “View usage”

Appendix B — Notes to self (cleanup)
- Ensure readout includes final D7 activation impacts in Week 4 consolidated analysis.
- Add a short segment breakdown next time (new users vs returning; SDK installed vs not; region).
